source.title: Diagnosing Batch Normalization in Class Incremental Learning
source.authors: Minghao Zhou; Quanziang Wang; Jun Shu; Qian Zhao; De-Yu Meng

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests BN effects on class-incremental learning, including sequential CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, rather than whether random-initialized networks reach near-zero training error. It evaluates related BN mechanisms in a new continual-learning setting.
record.gate_note: Results on accuracy, backward transfer, and feature representations in class-incremental learning do not measure training classification error or the training behaviors named in V1–V6. They are therefore not rows for those versions. The study reports variants comparing BN batch construction and statistics updating, plus BN Tricks against baselines; these results concern the paper's Class-IL method and are not included as claim rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses BN in ResNet-18 and compares BN updating strategies for class-incremental learning. Its outcomes are test accuracy, backward transfer and feature visualizations. It does not compare BN with no BN for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, or measure any other version's named training behavior.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that conventional BN usage can impair representation learning and bias classifiers in class-incremental learning, and propose BN Tricks to improve rehearsal-based methods. Reported ACC gains vary in size; BWT does not improve in every setting.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies BN strategies for class-incremental learning, not the training-error claim or the versions' stated recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The results vary with batch composition, EMA-statistics updating, buffer size, dataset and task sequence; the paper reports different ACC and BWT outcomes for ER, DER++, and iCaRL variants.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing BN batch composition and EMA updating changes class-incremental test accuracy and forgetting. In Table 2, ER-BNT achieves 72.08±0.55% ACC versus ER's 61.62±1.59%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Separating BN statistics updates from parameter updates and using balanced statistics batches can improve rehearsal-based class-incremental performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 changes only BN EMA statistics and shows classifier bias toward the last task; feature visualizations and ablations further diagnose representation overlap and training-inference discrepancy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN statistics and their training-inference discrepancy can affect classifier bias and forgetting in class-incremental learning.

record.problems: The results concern test accuracy and backward transfer in continual learning, not training classification error. Main benchmark results are averaged over 10 runs; no direct result tests the listed claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: All paper results are outside the claim versions: ACC/BWT comparisons and ablations concern class-incremental performance, and visualizations concern feature/classifier behavior. No rows were kept because none measures the claim's named training behavior.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including random labels, and dependence on size, stopping or regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
BN versus no-BN training speed and learning-rate tolerance; comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's tests/T3 classification with uses_without_test/T4. Its empty rows and labels are appropriate. Accuracy measured after successive tasks is test accuracy, not training classification error or a controlled measurement of BN-induced training acceleration.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error under SGD or Adam from random initialization, on CIFAR with corrupted or random labels; model size, stopping, and regularization effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and extra student width.
Depth effects on training error in plain versus residual networks.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Training loss and curvature dynamics at or above a stability learning-rate threshold.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance attributable to BN, including comparison with Fixup.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
